title: Oxygène
overview:
Recorded in Jarre's Paris apartment kitchen on Rue de la Trémoille — no studio time, no recording budget, no label commission. Six continuous parts that function as a single atmospheric statement about air, breath, and the texture of space. Key equipment: ARP 2600, EMS Synthi AKS, EMS VCS 3, Farfisa Professional Organ, Eminent 310 Unique (the atmospheric string sound), Korg Mini-Pops 7 drum machine, RMI Harmonic Synthesizer, Mellotron, and Michel Geiss's custom Rhytmi-computer. Produced and mixed with Jean-Pierre Janiaud.

Released December 1976 on Disques Motors / Polydor (France); initially 50,000 copies given free to hi-fi shops as a demonstration record. Grew to 15–18 million copies worldwide. Oxygène Part IV became the UK hit single. Won the Grand Prix du Disque. Timestamps approximate to ±5 seconds given the continuous-tape nature of the album's original recording.

tracks.title: Oxygène Part I
tracks.role: Album role: The album's opening atmospheric statement — establishing the sonic vocabulary before the famous melody of Part II enters. A lesson in patience: seven minutes of textural preparation as compositional discipline.

events.description: near-inaudible textural layer, expanding slowly. Not silence; something breathing.
events.detail: The apartment kitchen becomes infinite space. The entire album's philosophy announced in the first seconds.

events.description: the warm, slightly mournful sustained chord enters. The electric organ sound that defines the album's harmonic language.
events.detail: The Eminent 310 Unique is not a synthesizer but an electronic organ with a distinctive string-ensemble sound. Jarre uses it as a harmonic foundation throughout.

events.description: tentative, exploratory. Short phrases that do not yet commit to a theme.
events.detail: The ARP 2600 is a semi-modular analog synthesizer. Jarre patches it for these early melodic gestures — characteristic gliding tones.

events.description: discrete, muted. The mechanical heartbeat underneath the organic texture.
events.detail: The Mini-Pops 7 is a preset rhythm machine. Its slightly toy-like, deliberate quality becomes part of Jarre's aesthetic rather than a limitation.

events.description: the chord progressions begin moving. The static of the opening gives way to motion.
events.detail: The tension of Part I is the question: will the album remain atmospheric or commit to melody? Part II answers.

events.description: the texture prepares for the melodic arrival. A held chord resolves the anticipation.
events.detail: On the original vinyl, this is a continuous tape — no gap between parts. Part I's function is purely to make Part II's entry inevitable.

tracks.title: Oxygène Part II
tracks.role: Album role: The album's defining statement — the most recognised synthesizer melody of the 1970s. The arpeggiated ARP 2600 sequence over the Eminent 310 chord pad. Where Part I prepared, Part II delivers. The cultural centre of gravity for all electronic music in France.

events.description: the famous Oxygène Part II arpeggiated riff. A looping melodic pattern on the ARP 2600 sequencer, immediately recognisable.
events.detail: This single sequence launched an entire genre of electronic music. 1976 France: no precedent for an album-length purely instrumental synthesizer work selling at this scale.

events.description: the Eminent 310 pads shift chord, transforming the sequence's emotional character with each change.
events.detail: The genius of Part II: the same sequence sounds completely different as the harmonic foundation moves beneath it.

events.description: EMS Synthi AKS provides textural fills and atmospheric colours alongside the main sequence.
events.detail: The Synthi AKS (the briefcase version of the EMS Synthi A) is used for expressive ornamental elements throughout the album.

events.description: subtle changes in the sequence and harmonic palette. The piece develops without abandoning its central pulse.
events.detail: Repetition-with-development: the minimalist strategy that would define electronic music for decades.

events.description: maximum number of simultaneous elements. The apartment kitchen reaches its fullest imagined space.
events.detail: All tools of a one-man studio production: bouncing between tape machines, manual fader operation, no automation.

events.description: the sequence releases. The melody prepared; Part III will reset the palette.
events.detail: Part II is complete as a formal statement. What follows constitutes the more experimental, abstract side of the album.

tracks.title: Oxygène Part III
tracks.role: Album role: The album's briefest and most abstract section — an interlude between the two long melodic pieces either side of it. A palette-cleaning exploration using the EMS VCS 3's most unpredictable tonal qualities.

events.description: unusual timbres, pitch-unstable tones. The most avant-garde moment on the album.
events.detail: The VCS 3 is a British analog synthesizer known for its unpredictable, wobbly oscillators — Jarre uses this instability as a feature.

events.description: no melody, no conventional rhythm. Pure sound exploration.
events.detail: The shortest piece on the album is its most experimental. Its function is contrast. Side One ends here before the flip.

events.description: the section dissolves. Original vinyl Side One ends after Part III.
events.detail: Side Two opens with Part IV — immediately establishing a new character. The palindromic structure of the album places its two most melodic pieces (II and IV) as the outer frame of the abstract centre.

tracks.title: Oxygène Part IV
tracks.role: Album role: The UK hit single and the album's most commercially accessible piece — the signature hi-hat pattern and driving sequencer pulse make this the most "pop" moment. Its relative brevity (only 4:14 among the longer album sections) gives it a focused, single-like economy of form.

events.section: Driving hi-hat pattern — Side Two opens with momentum
events.description: the Korg Mini-Pops 7 provides a continuous eighth-note hi-hat pulse. The album's most rhythmically propulsive opening.
events.detail: Compared to Part I's patient atmospheric build, Part IV arrives briskly and purposefully. Side Two makes different demands on the listener — more kinetic.

events.description: a different melodic vocabulary from Part II. More chromatic, slightly unsettling but still highly listenable.
events.detail: The melody that became the UK single in 1977. Its recognisability is distinct from Part II's sequence — more explicitly contoured as a tune.

events.description: the chord sequence under the melody adds depth. RMI Harmonic Synthesizer contributes to the harmonic texture.
events.detail: The RMI Harmonic Synthesizer is an electromechanical instrument — interesting timbral texture between organ and synthesizer.

events.description: Part IV's complete production at its densest. The hit single earning its status.
events.detail: Chart position UK #65 on its original 1977 release — remarkable for an entirely instrumental electronic piece by a French composer.

events.description: the driving pulse eases. Part IV resolves cleanly before Part V's extended atmosphere.
events.detail: Part IV delivers the most compressed formal package on the album. Parts V and VI expand time again.

tracks.title: Oxygène Part V
tracks.role: Album role: The album's most expansive and diverse single section — over ten minutes traversing multiple textural territories. Part V contains the album's widest range of moods: meditative, urgent, ethereal, mechanical, and vast. The Mellotron appears here with its characteristic choral/orchestral illusion.

events.description: after Part IV's focused economy, Part V spreads outward. Wide synth pads, unhurried.
events.detail: The longest track earns its length by exploring what the shorter pieces could only suggest.

events.description: the strings/choir tape-replay instrument adds an orchestral warmth uniquely associated with 1970s progressive music.
events.detail: The Mellotron plays pre-recorded orchestral samples from tape — each key triggers a different tape strip. The result is recognisably artificial but hauntingly humanistic.

events.description: the Korg Mini-Pops reappears with a different pattern. The piece gains forward momentum.
events.detail: Multiple tempo zones within a single long section — the piece breathes differently in different moments.

events.description: the longest section reaches its highest intensity at midpoint. Multiple synthesizer voices active simultaneously.
events.detail: The cumulative density effect unique to Part V. No other section on the album sustains this much material for so long.

events.description: elements remove themselves one by one. Long release into texture.
events.detail: The reverse of the opening build — a slow withdrawal. Jarre respects the listener's need for space.

events.description: a final melodic gesture, quieter, reflective.
events.detail: The piece finds a different character in its final two minutes — more inward, preparing for Part VI's elegant conclusion.

events.description: the texture releases. The album's penultimate movement.
events.detail: Part V has covered the most ground. Part VI is the resolved, graceful landing.

tracks.title: Oxygène Part VI
tracks.role: Album role: The album's final statement — graceful, spacious, and harmonically resolving. Part VI returns to the atmospheric patience of Part I but now enriched by everything that has passed. The breath entering the body at the start now exhales fully.

events.description: unhurried, spacious. The album's accumulated tension releases into open sonic space.
events.detail: The final section mirrors the opening — both are atmospheric and melodically restrained. But Part VI carries all the preceding music's emotional weight.

events.description: a long, slow melodic line on a synthesizer voice. Not the urgency of Part II or IV — contemplative departure.
events.detail: The final melody of the album is its most resigned and beautiful. There is no need to assert anything — the album has already said what it needed to say.

events.description: modest by Part V's standards but emotionally fulfilling as a culminating gesture.
events.detail: The restraint of Part VI's peak is the point. This is the exhale after six parts of intake.

events.description: the last notes extend into silence. The synthesizers thin one by one.
events.detail: The air of the album's title disperses back into the atmosphere from which it was summoned. Circular structure: begins in near-silence, ends in near-silence.

events.description: the last tone fades.
events.detail: 15–18 million copies worldwide. Grand Prix du Disque. Recorded alone in a Paris apartment. The silence at the end contains all of that.
